tensions.name: DCPO occupies scalar code-confidence — is the direction still novel?

side_a.position: Training a code LLM to express calibrated discriminative scalar confidence (AUROC-measured) is now DONE by DCPO.
side_a.evidence: DCPO (ICML 2026) decoded <conf> block vs hybrid execution-pass-rate target; AUROC 0.796-0.914 on LiveCodeBench v5/v6 + HumanEval+, beats RLCR on AUROC and accuracy.

side_b.position: Prior code-calibration work either uses probes/no-AUROC (RLCM) or is QA-only (Rewarding Doubt), leaving genuine gaps.
side_b.evidence: RLCM uses hidden-state probe, never reports AUROC (grep-verified); Rewarding Doubt/ConfTuner AUROC 0.86 but QA-only.

tensions.resolution: Side A wins for the SCALAR framing — DCPO substantially occupies it, so a scalar headline is incremental. The residual novelty is the code-UNIQUE capability DCPO's single-scalar output cannot express: per-test-case / structured / localized confidence. The paper must pivot the headline there; scalar becomes a DCPO-positioned baseline. Step 8 must verify structured code-confidence is unoccupied.

tensions.name: Decouple architecturally vs. bounded joint reward

side_a.position: A single joint accuracy+confidence objective has a provable gradient conflict and collapses discrimination.
side_a.evidence: DCPO Prop 4.2 (gradient conflict for overconfident models); our own 274-example joint SFT collapsed to mean-0.900-everywhere; CAPO shows linear GRPO surrogate is AUC-inconsistent.

side_b.position: A well-chosen BOUNDED joint reward discriminates fine without decoupling, and is simpler/cheaper.
side_b.evidence: Rewarding Doubt: integrated (non-decoupled) log-score reward, AUROC 0.859, single A40 LoRA, beats a decoupled SFT probe on discrimination; RLCR proper-scoring theorem.

tensions.resolution: Adopt Side A (decouple) as the primary recipe because our documented collapse matches Prop 4.2's antecedent exactly, but run Side B (bounded joint reward) as the key ablation. Boundedness (Brier not log-score) is non-negotiable regardless — Beyond-Binary-Rewards' Toy-Arm experiment shows unbounded log-score reward-hacks into abstention-collapse under low signal.

tensions.name: NLI/embedding semantic equivalence fails on code — only execution works

side_a.position: Generic semantic-similarity (NLI, embeddings, CodeBLEU, AST) proxies collapse on code confidence.
side_a.evidence: Functional Entropy: NLI semantic entropy 0.47-0.58 (near chance) on code; Sharma&David: only symbolic-execution clustering restores signal, log-probs not significant; our AST proxy ECE 0.351.

side_b.position: Cheap structural/embedding proxies (MST clustering) give usable signal.
side_b.evidence: FASE embedding-clustering AUC 0.74-0.91, but with a blind spot on correlated-wrong collapse.

tensions.resolution: Side A: execution/functional equivalence is the only reliable label source for code confidence. This REINFORCES the method's use of per-test execution outcomes as ground truth — the labels are both free and uniquely trustworthy, which is precisely code's advantage over QA/math.

tensions.name: ECE-primary vs AUROC-primary evaluation

side_a.evidence: Most calibration papers (Multicalibration-for-code, 260113284) report ECE/BSS; Spiess uses ECE.

side_b.position: ECE alone is gameable by a near-constant predictor; report AUROC/discrimination.
side_b.evidence: Roelofs: ECE_bin biased; CAPO/Spiess: a constant predictor satisfies ECE (our collapse: mean 0.900 everywhere, low ECE, no discrimination); Multicalibration-for-code never reports AUROC and cannot show discrimination.

tensions.resolution: Side B decisively. The paper must make AUROC/discrimination (per-test AUROC for the headline) the PRIMARY metric, report debiased/adaptive ECE secondarily, and explicitly critique the ECE-only prior work — this is both methodologically correct and a positioning wedge against Multicalibration-for-code.

tensions.name: Is HumanEval's near-perfect oracle a contamination artifact?

side_a.position: HumanEval/MBPP contamination inflates results; the 0.987 oracle may be memorization.
side_a.evidence: Riddell 2024 + TRACER 2026: surface AND semantic 'shared-logic' contamination; models score higher on contaminated subsets.

side_b.position: The discrimination finding is robust on contamination-resistant benchmarks.
side_b.evidence: ConSelf replicates the difficulty-level disconnect on LiveCodeBench (post-training-cutoff problems) with the same model families.

tensions.resolution: Side B, conditional on design: the paper MUST evaluate primarily on LiveCodeBench (contamination-controlled, time-windowed) and treat HumanEval as a legacy comparison point only. This converts a threat into a robustness pillar.
